notes.title: Game Dev Update 4
notes.content:
Hi everyone and welcome another update on our game state.
 
As everyone says they have been hard at work, we have too. Another big leap forward in our matchmaking systems and overall stability of the game, magnifique as others would put it. 

Now as we have put forward the customary greetings we can get down to some interesting topics. The race in F1 Jeddah yesterday, quite the spectacle that one, has given another boost in the any story is a believable story thesis. Now whatever we say in our short story (-ies hopefully) should be met with that is about to be expected from a pinnacle motorsport. 

If the smack with a tuna shaped hint didn’t give it away, we are working on a shorty story to tie the first race in our game into the story world behind it. A prelude to which pair of racing boots you are stepping into and why they are they stuck 3 squares behind the leader, or why in fact you are the leader.  

There is a lot of work to be done on the story in both the writing and editing part, but work will continue nonstop (except for weekends off, national holidays and all things to make workloads humane of course) to get the story into your hands and crank the hype-engines for the upcoming game. 

This isn’t the only thing we want to do; we have a few more interesting things up our race-suit sleeve that are still too young for the spotlight. Be ready, be excited and if you haven’t get wishlisting (Both our game and other cool indie titles!)

Vlue

notes.title: Dev Update 3: Tearing and Ripping
notes.content:
Weeks are full of merry laughter is what we all wish developing a game was. There hasn’t been any major issues or any real issues at hand, but its always disheartening to see having to scrap some of your already made work. Even if it is inevitable. 

This time we had to scrap the in game UI as it didn’t fulfill its whole purpose. The idea was to have a combination of a steering while and old handheld console as the UI in game; A month or two removed from its inception it is now gone, awaiting its follow up. 

On a positive note we have had marked improvements on some online functionalities. Quite a few lines have been revamped to improve the experience. Now we can finally move on to adding more functions. In addition to the UI upgrade we upgrade our corner system, especially the effects of reaching a corner. There is hope we can show some preliminary footage of our upgrades in the coming week. 
Another thank you to everyone who is here and have another great week.

notes.title: Dev Update 2: One Click Experience
notes.content:
Greetings,

It is week two and it is time to talk about the one click game experience. Before we skim some of my thoughts, clear your mind with this childlike stand. (Alternatively titled giant pizza box eats crowd.)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41458549/e0a13aadea6fa118579cbef1eb343549127e968a.png
 
Everyone has played those games where it takes forever to get into the menu and there are way too many buttons to press before you are in your game. Click/wait through long introes at game startup; Click through the intro screen— the “press any button to proceed”; Click through the promotions and worst-case scenario you must search through menus, because it isn’t clear where you start the game. 
There are probably a few extra steps I am missing, but these are enough to be annoyed at.

My philosophy in this scenario is to reach as close to the one click threshold as possible. This threshold is something we do reach in Last Lap Heroes. After launching the game (if matchmaking solo) you only need one click to get in a match. 

Another complementary design choice is the maximum duration of a game. Knowing that you can get playing quickly and that there is a maximum duration for the game is a blessing. 
These two things are something I wish to keep in mind as I forge forward with developing this game with the rest of the team. 

CSG_Vlue

notes.title: Dev Update 1
notes.content:
A big thank you to the first ones here, we are very excited to share Last Lap Heroes with you. The game is coming along nicely, and we are hard at work in turning the Coming Soon button into a Buy Now! 
Our latest efforts have been in implementing the UI and we are starting to get quite happy it fits into the games theme. All the UI elements are quite loosely based off a formula steering wheel. 

Moving on from the status update— let us talk about Last Lap Heroes core loop. Your aim in almost every round is to reach the next corner without losing any or as little as possible Hit points.

To reach this goal you choose your gear, trying to have as many outcomes as possible inside the next corner. Based on your result you employ other mechanics like swerving, braking and tires to stop in the next corner safely. If you go over too far from the corner you will spin out, leaving you locked out of moving for a turn. 

The more brake, gear and tire points you have used in the game the more important every choice you make becomes. A game of risk-management and pushing your luck awaits you in the upcoming one evening beta test, Wishlist now to stay up to date.
